deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page (f.16) states the claims for an integer a. (I) Infinitely often frac(N e^{2/a}) < (1+eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN), and eventually always > (1-eps) times that. (II) For even a, the same two statements for 1 - frac(N e^{2/a}). (III) For odd a, the same for 1 - frac with 4|a| in place of |a|. This page proves the 'infinitely often' halves using continued-fraction convergents.

Step 1 (CF). Start from Lambert's continued fraction tanh x = x/(1+ x^2/(3+ x^2/(5+ ...))). Put x = 1/a and apply an equivalence transformation [mine]: tanh(1/a) = 1/(a + 1/(3a + 1/(5a + ...))). Since 1 - tanh y = 2/(e^{2y}+1) [mine], we get (6): (e^{2/a}+1)/2 = 1/(1 - 1/(a + 1/(3a + 1/(5a + ...)))).

Step 2 (convergents). Let u_n/v_n be the n-th convergent, with (7) u_1 = v_1 = 1, u_2 = |a|, v_2 = |a-1|. The recurrence (8) is w_{n+1} = w_{n-1} + (2n-1)|a| w_n. Check: u_2/v_2 = a/(a-1); u_3/v_3 = (3a^2+1)/(3a^2-3a+1). For a<0 rewrite as 1/(1 + 1/(|a| + 1/(3|a| + ...))), which gives the same recurrence with |a|.

Step 3 (error series). From the determinant identity u_{n+1}v_n - u_n v_{n+1} = ±1 [implicit], (9): (e^{2/a}+1)/2 = u_n/v_n + (-1)^{n-1}(1/(v_n v_{n+1}) - 1/(v_{n+1} v_{n+2}) + ...). This is valid as written for a>0.

Step 4 (growth). From (8), (10): v_{n+1} ~ (2n-1)|a| v_n ~ 2|a| n v_n, hence log v_n ~ n log n.

Step 5 (asymptotic error). Combining, (11): e^{2/a}+1 - 2u_n/v_n ~ 2(-1)^{n-1}/(v_n v_{n+1}) ~ (-1)^{n-1}/(|a| n v_n^2).

Step 6 (even a). All v_n are odd, since v_{n+1} ≡ v_{n-1} (mod 2). Take N = v_n; then n ~ logN/loglogN. Then N e^{2/a} = (2u_n - N) + error, with an integer first term, so (12): N(e^{2/a}+1) - 2u_n ~ (-1)^{n-1} loglogN/(|a| N logN). The two signs give the 'infinitely often' parts of (1) and (3).

Step 7 (odd a). Ramanujan asserts v_n is odd for n odd and even for n even. For n odd, N = v_n gives (13) with a + sign, i.e. frac small with constant 1/|a|. For n even, N = v_n/2 (u_n is then odd) gives N(e^{2/a}+1) - u_n = (v_n/2)(error) ~ -loglogN/(4|a| N logN), which is (14). That is 1 - frac small with constant 1/(4|a|), claim (5).

The page does not prove the lower-bound halves (2), (4), (6). Those need a best-approximation argument showing no other N does better.
errors: Sign error for negative a. The determinant u_2 v_1 - u_1 v_2 = |a| - |a-1| equals +1 for a>0 but -1 for a<0. So for a<0 the factor (-1)^{n-1} in (9), (11), (12), (13) should be (-1)^n. Example a = -1: (e^{-2}+1)/2 ≈ 0.5677 < u_1/v_1 = 1, yet (9) with n=1 would make it exceed 1.

Parity error for odd a. Mod 2 the recurrence is v_{n+1} ≡ v_{n-1} + v_n, a Fibonacci recurrence starting 1, 0. So v_n is even exactly when n ≡ 2 (mod 3), not when n is even. For a=3: v = 1, 2, 19, 287, 6046, ...; for a=1: v = 1, 0, 1, 5, 36, 329, ...

Consequence of the parity error. For odd a, even v_n occur with n odd (n ≡ 5 mod 6) as well as n even (n ≡ 2 mod 6). Taking N = v_n/2 with n odd gives frac(N e^{2/a}) ~ +loglogN/(4|a| N logN). This contradicts claim (2) of the previous page for odd a. Example a=1: N=18 gives 18 e^2 = 133.0030..., predicted 1/(4·5·18) ≈ 0.0028. For odd a both frac and 1-frac have lim-inf constant 1/(4|a|).

Incompleteness. Only the 'infinitely often' halves are argued. The lower bounds (2), (4), (6) on the previous page are not proved here; they need the best-approximation property of convergents and control of non-convergent N.
Degenerate case a=1: v_2 = |a-1| = 0, so the second convergent is infinite. This is harmless asymptotically but should be excluded.

results.what: Continued fraction (e^{2/a}+1)/2 = 1/(1 - 1/(a + 1/(3a + 1/(5a + ...)))), derived from the CF of tanh
results.modern_name: Lambert/Euler continued fraction for tanh; regular-type CF expansions of e^{2/a}

results.what: Convergent recurrence and error asymptotics: e^{2/a}+1 - 2u_n/v_n ~ (-1)^{n-1}/(|a| n v_n^2), log v_n ~ n log n
results.modern_name: Convergent asymptotics giving the irrationality measure function of e^{2/a}

results.what: Even a: ||N e^{2/a}|| < (1+eps) loglogN/(|a| N logN) infinitely often, from both sides (the a=2 case gives Davis's constant 1/2 for e)
results.modern_name: Davis-type sharp Diophantine approximation constant for e^{2/a}
results.usually_credited_to: C. S. Davis (1978) for e; Tasoev, Shiokawa, Elsner and others for e^{1/k}, e^{2/k}

results.what: Odd a: approximation constant 1/(4|a|), using N = v_n/2
results.modern_name: Sharp constant for e^{2/k}, k odd (lim inf N·logN/loglogN·||N e^{2/k}|| = 1/(4k))
results.usually_credited_to: Elsner and others (1990s-2000s); Ramanujan's version analysed by Berndt-Kim-Zaharescu (c. 2013)

deep.surprise_reason: To the best of my knowledge, this manuscript (Q.784 extension) is known and published in Ramanujan's Lost Notebook. I recall Berndt, Kim and Zaharescu analysing it, though I cannot confirm their exact findings. The results anticipate Davis (1978) and later work on e^{2/k}, but this anticipation is already recognised as Ramanujan's. The flawed parity argument for odd a is a detail a specialist would note, not a new attribution.

transcription_corrections: Header: 'Add. Ms a 94 18(17)', with folio number 17 circled.
'So is easy to deduce' should read 'It is easy to deduce'.
In (6) the CF is 1/(1-) 1/(a+) 1/(3a+) ..., i.e. 1/(1 - 1/(a + 1/(3a + ...))); the transcription is correct in content.
A pencil '?' in the left margin beside the 'a is odd and n is odd' line (possibly a later reader's doubt) is not transcribed.
